D10 APPROVED-FIX — date-only week counts mean 7 CALENDAR days, not 168 elapsed hours. D16 APPROVED-FIX — a 7-day forecast hit requires an eligible weigh-in on the due day or, failing that, the next day (one grace date); with no such reading the forecast is UNGRADED, not a miss; the day arithmetic follows D10. D25 APPROVED-FIX — "protein: good" requires at least one successful day within the current seven-logged-days window before the one-miss allowance applies; a first missed day cannot read "good". D32 APPROVED-FIX — "benefit replicated" counts only sessions from the CURRENT technique; all other replication thresholds stay as they are. D37 APPROVED-FIX — a merged earned receipt keeps the assessment as of the day it was earned, accepting that this can change whether a single-sighting increase counts as earned and the numbers printed on past earned receipts. D40 APPROVED-FIX — when two phones disagree on a day's calories with equal detail, ONE deterministic shared winner is chosen with the conflict kept visible and BOTH original entries retained; the exact tie-break rule and how the conflict is shown are NOT decided here and must be specified in the reviewed fix brief before anything is built. Totals: 45/45 dispositions recorded, 45 APPROVED-FIX, 0 KEEP, 0 DEFER, 0 UNRULED. What this does NOT do: it approves directions, not code — each theme still needs its accepted behaviour/delta brief, its red-first laws turning GREEN on the candidate and RED on the frozen engine, the post-fix gate's PACKAGE run and cowork's execution acceptance; the frozen app and its goldens stay untouched; no private release, spending, phone gate, remote gate or M2 closure is waived; no owner-specific interval or value is set. notes: SKELETON. B-LOM exists here so the runner admits the id and so the chain’s shape is visible; it declares no product, no child and no D-id, and every run of it is REVIEW-PENDING with the whole inventory open. Nothing in this file is a claim about the legacy order-mapping seam.

product is EMPTY on purpose: B-LOM’s parent is the B-NTC artifact, which is not sealed, so there is no parent product map to inherit and no pre-image to pin. The inventory is taken whole at B-NTC’s accepted head. While the parent is unsealed the runner cannot verify inventory completeness at all and says so in its own line.

coverage.inherited is EMPTY and children[] is empty for the same reason: inherited coverage IS the parent artifact’s own gate->child map byte-for-byte, and there is no parent artifact yet. All nineteen original gates re-execute under --full.

dIds and laws are empty because B-LOM is named in the runner’s NO_REGISTER_IDS set (DECISIONS:93). If the PM later rules that B-LOM does carry register repairs, the exemption is removed from b-package.cjs — not worked around here. THE REPLACEMENT OBLIGATION (TOOLING-REVIEW-r4 Y1): with no D-id there is no law accounting, so the runner requires at least MIN_OWN_CHILDREN declared child(ren) executing one of this package's own role:"new" product files. B-LOM declares none — product is {} and children[] is empty — so the run reports NO-REGISTER OBLIGATION 0 of 0, carries it as an OPEN obligation on top of the rest of the skeleton's, and the seal REFUSES with NO-REGISTER-PACKAGE-SEALED-WITHOUT-EXECUTING-ITS-OWN-PRODUCT. B-LOM cannot be sealed until it has a cell of its own that runs.
The brief is not written yet, so brief.sha256 is null and the runner leaves "brief not authored" OPEN.

PARENT, CORRECTED (TOOLING-REVIEW-r4 Y3). B-LOM’s ONLY parent option is B-NTC, which is not sealed, so this spec names no NATIVE-CARRIERS option and nothing here was re-pinned at the DECISIONS:104 CI re-seal. (The note that stood here through r3 said parent.options NATIVE-CARRIERS had been re-pinned; it was copied from B1/B2, where it is true, and this spec has no such option. Corrected rather than carried.) What IS re-taken at the tip is sourceBase e9c50e1; the parent pins are taken whole at B-NTC’s accepted head when it exists.

NO PRE-IMAGES TO RE-VERIFY (TOOLING-REVIEW-r4 Y3). product is {} — this spec pins no pre-image at all, so it makes no pre-image claim. The r3-era note that stood here described this spec's product pre-images as the parent's own pins carried forward; with an empty product map that said more than these bytes contain, so it is corrected rather than carried and the false sentence is not reproduced. When B-NTC seals, the inventory is taken whole from its artifact and re-verified by B-LOM’s own lane, not by the tooling fixer.

coverage.moves is {} and must stay {} (TOOLING-REVIEW-r3 X1): the runner refuses any non-empty moves while MOVES_RULING is absent, in spec() and again at the seal in envelope(). That is what closes r3’s R3-A — the move/needle composite reaches nothing at all when no move can be declared, rather than being narrowly bounded.

parent.options[].reviewSha256 pins the parent’s REVIEW file by bytes, and option() additionally requires the receipt base that review names to be an ancestor of refs/remotes/origin/rebuild/t2-client-core — resolved from Git refs, never from this spec (TOOLING-REVIEW-r3 X2, closing R3-B).

SINGLE PARENT, TWO WAYS (TOOLING-REVIEW-r4 Y2). parent.chosen is null here, so the rule is not yet engaged; when it is, parent() refuses if any sibling packages/*.json claims the same artifact — read BOTH from disk AND from Git at HEAD, so freeing a sibling’s `chosen` in an uncommitted edit no longer frees the parent (r4 G14) — and refuses again if an already-sealed rebuild/m4/spec/acceptance-*.json ON refs/remotes/origin/rebuild/t2-client-core names it. B-LOM’s only option is B-NTC, so the second head this guards against is a second claim on the B-NTC artifact once it exists.
